title: Paul McCartney attends the 13th Annual Grammy Awards | 1971
content:
Paul and Linda McCartney attended the 13th Annual Grammy Awards ceremony on 16 March 1971.

The ceremony was held at the Hollywood Palladium in Los Angeles, and was broadcast live for the first time. The host was Andy Williams.

The McCartneys were unsure as to whether attend, with Paul wanting to ensure that none of the other Beatles would be present. On the night, their limousine circled around the block several times until they felt confident enough to go inside.

Diane Brooks, who was working on marketing strategies for the Ram album, called the National Association of Recording Arts and Sciences (NARAS) to arrange tickets, and was told that Paul and Linda would be seated with Capitol Records execs near the front of the auditorium. Paul asked instead if they could have a table for five near the back, with places for Brooks and Denny and Monique Seiwell.

The Beatles received five nominations and won one award:

  • Won: Best Original Score Written for a Motion Picture or a Television Special – Let It Be
  • Nominated: Best Contemporary Vocal Performance By A Duo, Group Or Chorus – ‘Let It Be’
  • Nominated: Best Contemporary Song – ‘Let It Be’
  • Nominated: Record Of The Year – ‘Let It Be’
  • Nominated: Song Of The Year – ‘Let It Be’

The award was presented by John Wayne, who only announced John Lennon, Paul McCartney, and George Harrison. This was not his error – the list, supplied by NARAS, omitted Ringo Starr.

McCartney gave a brief interview and posed for press photographs after the presentation.

Page last updated: 13 November 2025
